problems.title: The quote depends on everyone finding time
problems.body: The site notes are in one place, the estimate in another and the design selections in a third. Someone has to reconcile all three before the client sees a price.

problems.title: The homeowner sees a number, not what it buys
problems.body: Your estimate and mood board arrive separately. The client struggles to connect the price to the finishes and rooms they imagined, so the next conversation becomes another explanation.

problems.title: A small finish change becomes a whole new evening
problems.body: The client swaps the cabinetry or stone. You update the allowance, the scope and the presentation—and check that the latest version still protects your margin.

deliverables.title: Build the next quote from the scope you already trust
deliverables.body: The agents prepare line items from your scope library, rate card and allowances. Missing costs and uncertain quantities are flagged for your estimator, so the draft follows your commercial rules.

deliverables.title: Show the interior concept beside the price
deliverables.body: Bring room concept sketches, material palettes and selected finishes into the same branded proposal as the quote. Your designer shapes the direction and approves generated concept imagery. Detailed construction drawings follow your normal design process.

deliverables.title: Give the homeowner one proposal to decide on

deliverables.title: Carry approved choices into the project
deliverables.body: Keep the accepted quote, selected finishes and open decisions together for the design and delivery team, so the project does not start by reconstructing the sales conversation.

workflow.title: Capture the renovation brief
workflow.body: Bring together the approved site notes, photographs, plans, client preferences and room list. Ask for missing measurements or choices instead of inventing them.

workflow.title: Build scope, design and price together
workflow.body: Prepare the room scope and concept pages, then match priced items to your approved rates and allowances. Keep optional upgrades separate from the base proposal.

workflow.title: Review the commercial and design details
workflow.body: The estimator checks quantities, supplier inputs and pricing. The designer reviews selections and visual concepts. Both can request a controlled revision.

workflow.title: Present the approved proposal
workflow.body: An authorized person approves release. Keep the final scope and design decisions available for the next sales conversation and project handoff.

title: AI property document review with source-linked findings.
description: For real estate law firms. We implement agentic solutions that compare property documents, flag discrepancies and put the supporting evidence beside each finding for attorney review.
lead: The client wants an answer. The unit description, plans and exhibits do not line up neatly, and the relevant amendment could be in another PDF. Before your attorney can assess the issue, someone has to find the right pages and repeat the comparison.
audience: You work in a U.S. boutique or midsize real estate law firm advising buyers or investors on property acquisitions.
You are the practice partner, real estate attorney or senior paralegal responsible for diligence and client updates.
Your team repeatedly compares similar document packages in a defined jurisdiction, with a qualified attorney responsible for the review.

problems.title: Every comparison means opening the same files again
problems.body: A unit description or parking reference appears across several documents. Each cross-check means finding the matching passage, exhibit and amendment before you can assess the difference.

problems.title: The summary still sends the attorney back to page one
problems.body: A note says there may be a discrepancy, but the supporting pages are missing. The attorney repeats the search to understand the issue and verify what the preparer found.

problems.title: An unanswered question becomes a late request
problems.body: A missing exhibit or unclear scan surfaces near the client deadline. Your team has to request clarification while explaining why the answer is still pending.

deliverables.title: Stop rebuilding the checklist for similar matters
deliverables.body: Your qualified reviewer defines the jurisdiction, eligible document package, fields to compare and questions that belong in the first version.

deliverables.title: Check a finding without hunting for its source
deliverables.body: A comparison table and findings with source references, pages and relevant excerpts or crops. Clearly distinguish supported matches, potential discrepancies and items not determined.

deliverables.title: Keep unresolved questions in view
deliverables.body: A concise list of conflicting facts, missing documents and questions for the attorney to assess. Prepare follow-up wording only after the responsible reviewer decides what to request.

deliverables.title: Explain the reviewed findings clearly to the client
deliverables.body: Turn the reviewed findings into the concise format your firm uses to explain the matter to its client. The attorney edits and approves the summary before release.

workflow.title: Check that the matter is eligible
workflow.body: Confirm the transaction type and jurisdiction, then verify the approved document set is complete and readable enough for the agreed checks.

workflow.title: Locate the facts and their counterparts
workflow.body: Extract the specified identifiers, descriptions and attachments. Find the relevant passages or plan areas in the other approved sources.

workflow.title: Prepare the evidence and open questions
workflow.body: Assemble the comparison report, preserve conflicting sources and flag anything the supplied documents cannot establish.

workflow.title: Review and explain the result
workflow.body: The attorney evaluates significance, corrects the draft and approves any requests or client summary. The system does not clear the transaction.

example.label: ILLUSTRATIVE EXAMPLE
example.title: The parking reference does not line up across the file.
example.body: A buyer’s counsel reviews a condominium package using a locally approved checklist. A parking reference in one document differs from the corresponding exhibit. The workflow places both sources in the draft report and flags an unclear amendment. The attorney checks the evidence, determines whether the difference matters and decides which clarification to request.
example.input: The attorney-selected transaction documents, relevant plans and exhibits, and the jurisdiction-specific comparison checklist.
example.output: A source-linked comparison, the conflicting parking references, the unresolved amendment question and a draft matter summary.
example.reviewer: The responsible real estate attorney interprets the documents, decides the legal significance and approves client-facing work.

systems.body: Use the matter folders and document-management process your firm approves. We define where the source files are read, where drafts are stored and which team members can review them.
items: Firm diligence checklists and report templates
systems.footnote: The initial offer uses documents your team selects. Public-record retrieval and additional jurisdictions require separate validation. Legal opinions and transaction decisions remain with the responsible professionals.

title: AI intake and case workflows for immigration law firms.
description: We implement agentic solutions that turn approved intake notes into the right questionnaires, document requests and case tasks, with attorney approval and connections to your existing tools.
lead: The consultation is over, but the client is still waiting for the next step. Someone needs to confirm the case type, choose the right questionnaire, prepare the document request and update the case system. When that handoff depends on one busy person, the whole team waits.
audienceTitle: For immigration partners and the teams keeping cases moving.
audience: You run a U.S. immigration law firm with repeat family, employment or investor case workflows.
You are the managing partner, operations manager or senior paralegal responsible for intake, case preparation and client follow-up.
Your team uses a case system, email and shared files, but still copies information and chases the next step by hand.
painTitle: The work between the legal decisions keeps piling up.
painIntro: Your attorneys know which work needs their judgment. Routine handoffs, missing documents and disconnected status updates keep pulling them back into administration.

problems.title: A good consultation becomes a slow start
problems.body: The intake notes are ready, but selecting the right document pack and drafting the next email still sits in someone’s queue. The client calls again because they do not know what to send.

problems.title: The same facts are entered in several places
problems.body: A client’s details move from the consultation notes to a questionnaire, case record, engagement letter and billing system. Every handoff creates another place to check and correct.

problems.title: Case status lives with the person who last touched it
problems.body: The office has to search email, spreadsheets and case notes to answer a client, find a missing document or establish who owns the next action.

serviceLine: FutureProof builds and implements agentic solutions around your firm’s actual case workflows. Built with security in mind, with controlled access and human approval.

deliverables.title: Prepare the next step while the intake is still fresh
deliverables.body: Turn approved consultation notes and a staff-confirmed case type into the appropriate questionnaire, document checklist and draft client message. Your team reviews the pack before anything goes out.

deliverables.title: Give each case a clear owner and next action
deliverables.body: Keep approved case details, received documents, missing items and assigned tasks together. Show what needs attention without making staff reconstruct the case from email.

deliverables.title: Keep scheduling and billing connected to the matter
deliverables.body: Where supported, connect consultation bookings, engagement status and invoice follow-up to the case record. Define approvals and reconcile exceptions with the team that owns the work.

deliverables.title: Expand after the first workflow proves useful
deliverables.body: Add attorney-reviewed form preparation, case reporting, office routines or a broader custom platform in agreed stages. Migration from an existing case system gets its own export, validation and acceptance plan.

workflow.title: Confirm the intake and case type
workflow.body: Use the sources and consent process your firm approves. An authorized team member confirms the matter type, required templates and the scope of the next step.

workflow.title: Prepare the document pack
workflow.body: Assemble the correct questionnaire, checklist, engagement draft and follow-up message. Flag missing or conflicting facts for a person to resolve.

workflow.title: Review before sending
workflow.body: The assigned reviewer checks recipients, case details and wording. Approved communication is sent through the firm’s supported tools and recorded with the case.

workflow.title: Track the work that follows
workflow.body: Update the checklist as documents arrive, surface agreed deadlines and assign outstanding tasks. Attorneys remain responsible for legal decisions, final documents and filings.

example.label: ILLUSTRATIVE WORKFLOW
example.title: The client knows what to send after the consultation.
example.body: After a consultation, the attorney confirms the case type and records the agreed next steps. The workflow selects the firm’s approved questionnaire and document checklist, drafts the client email and creates tasks for the case team. A paralegal checks the pack, the designated reviewer approves it and the case record shows what was requested and what is still missing.
example.input: Approved intake notes, a confirmed case type, current firm templates and the client details your team has checked.
example.output: A draft questionnaire and document request, assigned case tasks and a record of approved client communication.
example.reviewer: The responsible attorney or authorized team member approves the pack. Legal eligibility, advice and filing decisions stay with the attorney.

faqs.q: Is this a new software subscription?
faqs.a: It is an implementation service. We map the workflow, build the agents and connections, test them with your team and support the agreed rollout. A broader custom platform is a separate scope when that fits your firm.

faqs.q: Can you work with our current CRM and case tools?
faqs.a: We build around your existing setup where access is supported. During mapping, we check software plans, permissions and integration options before committing to a connection or migration.

faqs.q: How do you handle confidential case information?
faqs.a: We agree which records the workflow may access, who can review drafts and which providers and retention settings your firm permits. Access controls and approval steps are tested before live use.

faqs.q: Will an agent give legal advice or file applications?
faqs.a: The offer supports preparation and office operations. Attorneys own legal advice, eligibility assessments, final review and filing. Any official system connection needs separate validation and authorization.

faqs.q: How fast can our office use it?
faqs.a: We set the rollout plan after mapping one workflow and confirming access. The pilot measures preparation and review together. Timing depends on the scope, templates, integrations and availability of your reviewers.

cta.title: Where does a new case get stuck after the consultation?
cta.body: Talk through one intake-to-document handoff with Yuval. We’ll look at the tools, the approval steps and a focused first implementation for your firm.

workflow.title: Review and follow through

faqs.q: Who is this for?
